messages:
Ivy: GateBank reported after migrating to Redwood Private via Azure Private Link they intermittently get TLS certificate mismatch and occasional 502s. Happened after creating the private endpoint and linking the Private DNS zone. Can someone triage?
Ethan: Hi Ivy — I'm GateBank infra. We made a Private Endpoint to our service alias in Redwood's subscription, enabled private DNS integration into our vnet, and linked the privatedns zone to the VNet. Some app instances resolve to 10.0.48.7 (PE NIC) and succeed, others resolve to the public frontend (40.78.x.x) and see cert CN=frontdoor.azure.com. Timeouts occur from certain subnets only.
Sofia: Quick checklist: 1) confirm private endpoint NIC IPs are the ones you expect (az network private-endpoint show). 2) check VNet DNS resolution path — are some hosts using corporate DNS forwarder? 3) any Azure Firewall or corporate proxy doing TLS inspection?
Ethan: Ran `az network private-endpoint show -g rbw-prod -n rbw-pe` -> shows NIC ip 10.0.48.7. VMs in subnet-a resolve to 10.0.48.7, VMs in subnet-b resolve to 40.78.x.x. Subnet-b uses a custom DNS server (10.10.10.5) from DHCP options. Also we have Azure Firewall in a hub vnet and route tables sending 0.0.0.0/0 through it for subnet-b. Firewall is configured with TLS inspection enabled.
Marco: That smells like split-horizon DNS + TLS inspection. If a host resolves to public IP but traffic is routed through Firewall that does TLS intercept, you'll see Front Door certs or firewall certs. Intermittent 502s may also be caused by SNAT / port exhaustion on the firewall for many simultaneous connections.
Ivy: On one failing VM I ran `nslookup api.private.redwood-inference.com` -> answer 40.78.x.x. On a passing VM it was 10.0.48.7. We don't have a private hosted zone in the customer's subscription, we used the Private DNS zone provided by Redwood and linked it. Could the link not be applied to that subnet?
Sofia: When you link a private DNS zone, the link is at the VNet level. Check `az network private-dns link vnet list -g rg` to ensure the VNet for subnet-b is listed and in 'Enabled' state. Also check /etc/resolv.conf or the VM's DNS settings — if the VM is configured to use the corporate DNS (10.10.10.5), the forwarder might not forward queries to Azure DNS (168.63.129.16).
Ethan: `az network private-dns link vnet list` shows our prod-vnet linked for subnet-a but not for subnet-b (we missed adding it when provisioning). So DNS is the cause for that subnet. But why TLS inspection causes timeouts even when DNS resolves to PE IP?
Marco: Two possibilities: 1) Azure Firewall performing TLS inspection will terminate TLS and present its own cert if Inspect TLS is enabled — that causes mismatch unless your trust chain includes the firewall CA. 2) If traffic to the private endpoint still traverses the firewall (asymmetric routing) it might be SNAT'd and return traffic won't route back to the private endpoint ENI, leading to resets. Private Endpoint traffic should stay within the VNet and not go to firewall for private IPs; confirm your UDRs for the subnet don't direct traffic to firewall for the PE IP range.
Sofia: Repro steps for you to gather logs: 1) From a failing VM: `dig +short api.private.redwood-inference.com` and `curl -v --resolve 'api.private.redwood-inference.com:443:10.0.48.7' https://api.private.redwood-inference.com/health` 2) tcpdump on NIC to confirm packet path `sudo tcpdump -nn -i eth0 host 10.0.48.7 and port 443` 3) check firewall logs for connections from VM IP to 10.0.48.7 and whether the firewall is inspecting them.
Ethan: Ran `curl -v` with --resolve to 10.0.48.7: returns 200 and correct cert SAN. Regular curl without resolve on same host sometimes returns 502 or cert CN frontdoor.azure.com. Tcpdump shows packets leaving the subnet and hitting the firewall IP 10.1.0.4 before they reach the PE NIC.
Ivy: So two issues: DNS link missing for subnet-b (fix: add private DNS zone link for that VNet) and UDR forcing traffic to firewall for private endpoint IPs (fix: add route exemptions or adjust UDR to ensure traffic to PE NIC IPs uses default VNet routing). Any recommended guidance for customers who must have firewall inspection policy?
Marco: If inspection is mandatory, best practice is to exempt Private Endpoint ENI CIDRs from TLS inspection and SNAT on the firewall so TLS to those private IPs remains passthrough. Also consider using service tags or firewall rules to bypass inspection for the target PE IPs. Alternatively, run a split DNS where only the private name resolves to PE IPs for all VNets and ensure resolvers are consistent.
Sofia: On our side, confirm the Private Link service accepted the connection (Redwood should see the private endpoint connection as Approved/Connected) and NLB/backend health is green. We'll also surface any per-consumer TLS-inspect metrics.
Ethan: Action items: 1) We'll add the private DNS link for subnet-b and flush DNS caches on VMs. 2) Update UDRs so PE IPs are not routed to Firewall, and request SecOps to exempt PE CIDR from TLS inspection/SNAT. 3) Ivy, can you verify the endpoint connection acceptance in Redwood console?
Ivy: Verified: endpoint connection accepted and backend health OK. We'll also add a dashboard widget to monitor per-consumer TLS handshake failures and 502 rates.
support-bot: Ticket #INC-5821 updated: root cause: split-horizon DNS (missing private DNS link) + Azure Firewall TLS inspection and UDR-based asymmetric routing causing cert mismatches and intermittent timeouts. Recommended fix: link Private DNS to all VNets, exempt PE CIDRs from TLS inspection and SNAT, ensure routing keeps private traffic local.
Ethan: Thanks all — after adding DNS link and firewall exemptions, our tests show consistent 200s and correct certs. Closing once SecOps applies exemptions to remaining subnets.
Ivy: Marking as resolved pending SecOps confirmation. Thanks!
